request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "My crew due total" (`my-crew-due-total`). It adds up the due totals of every crew led by the signed-in user's person, and stays blank if no person has the user's name or none of them leads a crew. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This was a front-end-only change. The data it needs (crews, each crew's due total, and finding "my" person) was already there, so the server and stored data are unchanged and nothing new is written to the audit file.

- **`src/main/frontend/features/header/totals.ts`**: added `useMyCrewDue`. It works out each crew's figure the same way the crew rows do (`crewDueTotal`), so the header always agrees with them. I also moved the existing "find the user's person" code (matches name or alias, ignoring case) into a small `findUser` helper so "my due total" and the crew total use the same rule. That's why a user signed in as "uma" counts as Cam, who has the alias "Uma".
- **`src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`**: shows the new value after "My overdue total".

If the person leads several crews and someone is in more than one of them, that person's due is counted once per crew. "Added up" in the request reads that way, and none of the tests cover it.
